post.title: Waiting one month? People demanded a 345% yearly rate
post.ig:
Waiting one month? People demanded a 345% yearly rate.

In Richard Thaler's 1981 survey, the median person wanted $20 in a month to give up $15 now. Over 10 years, the implied rate fell to about 19% a year.
That's present bias: "now" gets full value, everything later gets an extra discount (David Laibson, 1997).
In a 2011 study (Hershfield et al.), people shown an aged photo of themselves put about twice as much of a hypothetical $1,000 toward retirement.
With Save More Tomorrow, joiners at one company went from saving 3.5% to 13.6% of pay in 40 months (Thaler & Benartzi, 2004).

Sources: Thaler, Economics Letters 1981; Laibson, QJE 1997; Hershfield et al., JMR 2011; Thaler & Benartzi, JPE 2004.
